title: Black Cat
summary: Black Cat / Portable Trusted Linux has an exact M13B physical-test candidate after the report-permission fix and compact boot-branding repair. The integrated self-hosted build and UEFI/QEMU smoke gates passed, and the candidate identity remains frozen below. The repository-canonical project viewer is fail-closed, protected-token-file only and temporarily pinned to the authoritative M13B branch. Builder/server telemetry remains display-only and separate from GitHub authority. AI autonomy and continuity are repository-governed through AI_AUTONOMY_POLICY.md and compact AI_WORK_STATE.md. The reusable continuity/context-recovery pattern and empirical GREEN/AMBER/RED calibration remain published for other projects. Future M26 native Black Cat AI project automation is now baked into the repository as concrete design scaffolding: templates/ai-project contains a provider-neutral reusable project seed, schema/ai-project-policy.schema.json defines the first machine-readable capability-policy contract, and static checks preserve conservative defaults such as HUMAN_GATE, no root/raw-device/credential access and no inbound listener. This scaffold is inert design material until M26 after M25, so it does not displace the active trust-chain roadmap or grant new runtime authority. The proposed inbound webhook/controller automation remains superseded before deployment, and the separate Approved Black Cat ISO release gate remains closed.

candidate.note: TEST CANDIDATE — NOT AN APPROVED RELEASE. This is the corrected M13B image selected for physical USB retest. The integrated build, UEFI menu smoke and automatic Black Cat quick-check smoke passed. GitHub sign-in with repository read access may be required to download the Actions artifact ZIP. After extraction, verify the ISO is exactly 376,438,784 bytes and SHA-256 cb14d25b7fd43e2b0e563efaada357d6ab196a42d717b016c4857f85968fe641 before writing the spare USB. Physical validation is still pending.

sections.title: Automation Manifesto — proceed by default
sections.content: Black Cat engineering proceeds automatically through safe, reversible, auditable, already-authorized work. Human interruption is reserved for physical hardware interaction, destructive or difficult-to-reverse actions, platform/trust-ownership changes, new credentials or authorization, secret exposure risk, financial/legal/public-release commitments, material security-policy choices, or essential information that genuinely cannot be derived safely.

sections.title: AI autonomy policy — when GPT continues automatically
sections.content: AI_AUTONOMY_POLICY.md at the repository root is the canonical operational decision table. AUTO actions proceed without routine confirmation. AUTO_WITH_CHECKS actions proceed when their stated safety/regression checks pass. HUMAN_GATE actions stop for the operator, including physical/destructive device work, trust-ownership changes, new credentials/permissions, merges to main, approved-release promotion, new Internet-facing services and material security-policy choices. FORBIDDEN_BY_DEFAULT actions include secret exposure and weakening security gates for convenience. Missing tool capability is a capability boundary rather than a policy approval requirement.

sections.title: Recoverable AI chat continuity and context health
sections.content: AI_WORK_STATE.md is the compact first-read recovery checkpoint for fresh sessions or uncertain continuity. Ordinary continuing turns do not bulk-load repository history. Recovery verifies only volatile branch/CI/artifact facts required for the next action and loads policy, technical and lesson files selectively. Context pressure is never presented as an exact hidden ChatGPT context percentage; GREEN/AMBER/RED is a heuristic based on observable proxies such as turns, large reads, tool-heavy operations, pasted material and continuity symptoms. AMBER/RED checkpointing is automatic work, not a human gate. docs/13-ai-continuity-and-context-recovery.md publishes the reusable method and docs/14-context-health-calibration-log.md records real events so the heuristic can improve empirically.

sections.title: Future native AI project automation in Black Cat Linux
sections.content: After M25, planned M26 turns the repository-governed automation pattern into a native Black Cat user-space project facility. The design is already concretely scaffolded in templates/ai-project plus schema/ai-project-policy.schema.json. A future project template/CLI creates rules, autonomy policy, compact work state, lessons, decisions and a machine capability profile. A deterministic autonomy engine and sandboxed operating-system capability broker enforce filesystem, Git, build/test, network, device and privilege boundaries independently of the model. The checked-in sample policy deliberately defaults to HUMAN_GATE with network disabled, no inbound listener, no root/raw-device/credential access and explicit forbidden secret/safety/self-expansion actions. Model adapters remain provider-neutral, with local-first/offline operation preferred and remote providers optional. Background continuation uses user-level systemd services/timers or outbound-only checks, not a new public listener. A dashboard shows project state, Context Health, diffs, audit summaries and exact human gates. Adversarial tests cover prompt injection, policy/schema mismatch, credential access, unsafe shell/device requests and corrupted recovery state. This scaffold is inert until M26 and must not delay M13B→M25 core security work.

sections.title: Zero-new-inbound automation policy
sections.content: The earlier cPanel webhook/controller proposal was superseded before deployment. No webhook endpoint, public controller, OpenAI API key or autonomous GitHub-writing service was deployed. Existing GitHub Actions remain the default automation infrastructure. If unattended reconciliation becomes necessary, prefer an outbound-only watchdog outside public_html. A new listener, writable endpoint, credential or API integration requires a separate security justification showing that its benefit outweighs the attack surface it creates.

sections.title: Black Cat visual identity and boot branding
sections.content: The current boot splash is a compact 160x120, 8-colour PNG stored as repository-controlled base64 text. The decoded splash SHA-256 is 24d03a442c3f7f04a060d30fbf8710f8b8cd2b5495caffdeea7cc47fcbc546ea. Build preparation requires successful decode and exact digest before staging the image for GRUB/UEFI and Syslinux/legacy. Branding remains cosmetic and cannot determine trust or boot eligibility.

sections.title: Branding boundary
sections.content: Black Cat is the user-facing project/product name. Portable Trusted Linux remains the technical description and PTL remains the stable internal engineering shorthand in repository paths, PTL_ variables, workflows and existing evidence identifiers.

sections.title: Current focus
sections.content: All active engineering is focused on Black Cat / Portable Trusted Linux Prototype 1. Community Compute Commons remains paused.

sections.title: Core trust chain
sections.content: Authenticated release reference -> verified USB image -> UEFI/Secure Boot -> measured boot and TCG event log -> TPM PCR evidence -> signed UKI -> authenticated dm-verity root -> immutable Linux -> RAM-backed disposable state -> nonce-bound TPM Quote -> independent verifier -> attestation report.

sections.title: Current Test Candidate versus Approved ISO
sections.content: The viewer exposes one exact Current Test Candidate only when filename, byte size, SHA-256, source commit, build run, artifact identity, HTTPS artifact link and passed automated smoke state are all present. It is explicitly labelled TEST CANDIDATE — NOT AN APPROVED RELEASE. The separate Approved Black Cat ISO gate remains closed until deliberate promotion and later release-authenticity controls.

sections.title: Canonical fail-closed project viewer
sections.content: The cPanel-hosted viewer accepts the GitHub read-only credential only from /home/learning/.blackcat/github_token. The enclosing directory and token file must have no group/world permission bits. No environment-variable, hard-coded-token or authoritative offline-cache fallback is accepted. While PR #6 contains the authoritative M13B state, the viewer is temporarily pinned to codex/remove-chroot-systemd-boot rather than stale main. After merge, the viewer and its regression test return to main together.

sections.title: Operational status versus project authority
sections.content: The living viewer may read project_cache/builder_status.json only for display-only builder/server telemetry. It is not an authoritative fallback and cannot enable or alter test-candidate or approved-release state. Project, candidate and release metadata remains live GitHub API data from the canonical development branch, and the viewer presents the authority/source details in a separate Project Data Source panel.

sections.title: Current automated rebuild evidence
sections.content: GitHub Actions run 34686464650 completed successfully for source commit c56389b71ecd96270bdd047369378f5a94d8bf93. The self-hosted job built and fingerprinted the Debian Live ISO, and the integrated hosted smoke job verified the embedded Black Cat menu, reached the UEFI menu and automatically reached the Black Cat quick-check marker in live userspace. Artifact 10300658965 is the frozen M13B physical-test artifact.

sections.title: CI concurrency discipline
sections.content: PR workflow path filters can retrigger builds because the PR already contains build/config/workflow changes. Per-PR concurrency collapses obsolete work. Hosted/read-only jobs may cancel superseded in-progress copies; the self-hosted live-build preserves an active chroot build and only collapses pending duplicates.

sections.title: Physical System Check result
sections.content: The previous candidate physically reached the no-typing Black Cat System Check and displayed observations without operator command entry, but exposed Permission denied on report writes. That older candidate remains superseded evidence. The source fix makes systemd the sole report producer and the login hook display-only; the new candidate must now receive one physical retest.

sections.title: Duplicate diagnostic execution fix
sections.content: blackcat-check.service is the sole root-owned evidence producer. The login/profile hook waits for and displays the service-generated report only. Static checks reject any future direct collector invocation from the profile hook.

sections.title: Evidence classification
sections.content: The quick-check screen reports observations and does not become its own ultimate verifier. Individual observations remain OBSERVED/UNKNOWN/etc. until stronger cryptographic and independent verification gates are implemented.

sections.title: Verified builder toolchain
sections.content: The remote Debian 13 builder has the declared live-build, xorriso, verity, UKI, signing and TPM tooling installed. It remains a builder rather than an attestation target because the cloud VM does not expose the required UEFI/TPM interfaces.

sections.title: Current candidate provenance
sections.content: The selected M13B physical-test ISO is live-image-amd64.hybrid.iso, exactly 376438784 bytes, SHA-256 cb14d25b7fd43e2b0e563efaada357d6ab196a42d717b016c4857f85968fe641, from source commit c56389b71ecd96270bdd047369378f5a94d8bf93, workflow run 34686464650 and artifact 10300658965. Artifact-container digest and ISO digest are different identities and must not be confused.

sections.title: Immediate evidence gate
sections.content: M13B remains current. Automated rebuild and UEFI/QEMU gates have passed for the exact candidate. The next genuine human gate is physical: download and verify the exact ISO, raw-write it to the clean spare USB, boot Black Cat - System Check without typing commands, confirm there are no Permission denied errors, photograph the result and verify internal disks remain unmounted by default.

sections.title: Progressive hardening
sections.content: Prototype stages may temporarily use weaker controls to prove the workflow, but every such control must document its trust assumption, compromise path, temporary justification and stronger replacement. Bootstrap credentials, the self-hosted runner, the cPanel read-only repository token, GitHub Actions artifact distribution and temporary live-build privilege are not final security controls; signing keys must never be placed in the viewer credential path.

sections.title: Mandatory lessons discipline
sections.content: Every meaningful session updates docs/07-lessons-learned.md and affected specifications or decisions. AI_WORK_STATE.md is refreshed when material handoff/context state changes, and project_content.json is always written last.

decisions.title: Reuse mature security components
decisions.text: Use Debian, UEFI Secure Boot, systemd UKI, TPM 2.0 and dm-verity rather than inventing replacement primitives.

decisions.title: Independent verification is mandatory
decisions.text: The target computer cannot be the sole authority deciding that its own measurements are trustworthy.

decisions.title: GitHub is the canonical development workspace
decisions.text: Documents, source and the living JSON index are versioned in the private repository.

decisions.title: Lessons learned are mandatory output
decisions.text: Every meaningful engineering/research session records lessons before project_content.json is updated last.

decisions.title: Prototype 1 baseline is Debian 13/trixie amd64
decisions.text: Exact build-host and package versions are captured as provenance.

decisions.title: Community Compute Commons paused
decisions.text: The research remains preserved, but active implementation returns exclusively to the core trust chain until its initial acceptance gates pass.

decisions.title: Progressive hardening is mandatory
decisions.text: Temporary weaker controls may be used to make demonstrable progress only when their assumptions, weaknesses and stronger replacements are explicit. They must never be presented as final security controls.

decisions.title: Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner is the initial remote execution path
decisions.text: Repository-scoped Actions jobs provide the auditable control path into the disposable build VM. Privileged operations remain explicitly separated from the unprivileged runner.

decisions.title: Build host and attestation target are separate roles
decisions.text: The DigitalOcean VM is used for building and artifact generation. UEFI measured-boot and TPM attestation claims require a separate platform that exposes those interfaces.

decisions.title: Normalize builder capability checks
decisions.text: Host preflight uses a deterministic system PATH so service-account environment differences cannot silently hide installed administrative tools.

decisions.title: Privilege only the live-build construction stage
decisions.text: Live-build preparation is unprivileged. The actual lb build operation is the current explicit privileged boundary and any passwordless permission used for Prototype 1 is temporary, documented and subject to later hardening.

decisions.title: Record source identity separately from checkout identity
decisions.text: CI manifests record intended source commit/ref separately from the temporary merge/detached checkout identity that a pull-request workflow may use.

decisions.title: Black Cat is the user-facing brand
decisions.text: Keep PTL internal engineering identifiers stable while presenting the product/project to users as Black Cat.

decisions.title: No-typing hardware diagnostics
decisions.text: Provide a dedicated Black Cat System Check boot menu entry that automatically collects modular runtime observations and presents a photograph-friendly screen.

decisions.title: Physical boot is an observation, not attestation
decisions.text: A successful USB boot proves bootability on the tested configuration only and must not be promoted to Secure Boot, TPM, dm-verity, firmware or release-authenticity assurance.

decisions.title: Approved releases are separate from CI candidates
decisions.text: The public project viewer only exposes an approved ISO after one exact candidate is deliberately promoted and its filename, byte size, SHA-256, source identity and test state are recorded. This reduces operator error but does not replace future cryptographic release signing.

decisions.title: Public viewer uses one protected read-only credential file
decisions.text: The cPanel-hosted viewer accepts only /home/learning/.blackcat/github_token, outside the public web root, with private permissions. Missing or unsafe credential state fails closed; no environment, hard-coded or cache fallback is accepted. This credential is repository-read only and must never be reused as a signing trust root.

decisions.title: UEFI QEMU tests use explicit OVMF pflash state
decisions.text: Boot-smoke workflows pair a non-secboot OVMF CODE image with its matching writable VARS template through pflash drives. Firmware-launch failures remain separate from ISO-build evidence.

decisions.title: PR workflows use evidence-aware concurrency
decisions.text: Hosted/read-only jobs cancel superseded PR copies. The self-hosted live-build preserves an active run but collapses older pending duplicates, avoiding unsafe mid-build interruption while prioritizing the newest candidate revision.

decisions.title: Current Test Candidate is separate from Approved ISO
decisions.text: The viewer may expose one exact smoke-passed GitHub Actions artifact for operator physical testing, clearly labelled TEST CANDIDATE — NOT AN APPROVED RELEASE. Approved release distribution remains a separate promotion state.

decisions.title: Systemd is the sole Black Cat quick-check evidence producer
decisions.text: Physical testing showed that executing the collector again from the normal-user profile hook conflicts with root-owned /run/blackcat reports. The systemd service now produces evidence exactly once; the login hook is display-only and static tests enforce that boundary.

decisions.title: Automation Manifesto pre-pause check is mandatory
decisions.text: Safe reversible auditable in-scope work proceeds automatically. Human interruption is reserved for physical, destructive/irreversible, authorization, trust-ownership, secret, commitment, material-policy or genuinely unresolved-information gates.

decisions.title: Boot branding is reproducible but cosmetic
decisions.text: Black Cat boot imagery is staged from repository-controlled bytes with a pinned SHA-256 and independent static decode check. Inability to render it must never alter trust classification or remove ordinary boot choices.

decisions.title: Decode before digest for text-encoded binary assets
decisions.text: Boot-image preparation validates source existence, successful base64 decode and then exact decoded SHA-256 before staging any branding bytes.

decisions.title: Automation convenience must not create new inbound attack surface by default
decisions.text: The webhook/controller proposal was superseded before deployment. Existing GitHub Actions remain the default; outbound-only reconciliation is preferred if unattended monitoring becomes necessary. New listeners, credentials or API integrations require separate security justification.

decisions.title: Canonical viewer and candidate record are regression-guarded
decisions.text: The production viewer is deployed only from web/project.php, accepts only the protected token file, serves no authoritative offline cache, and temporarily reads the authoritative M13B branch. Static checks require the Current Test Candidate panel and prevent M13B from silently losing its candidate record.

decisions.title: Operational telemetry is display-only
decisions.text: The viewer may render local builder/server status from project_cache/builder_status.json, but local telemetry cannot substitute for GitHub authority or alter candidate/release gates. Source identity and authority are shown separately in a clear Project Data Source panel.

decisions.title: Root AI autonomy policy is the operational continue/stop authority
decisions.text: AI_AUTONOMY_POLICY.md at the repository root classifies actions as AUTO, AUTO_WITH_CHECKS, HUMAN_GATE or FORBIDDEN_BY_DEFAULT. Routine safe engineering proceeds automatically; merges to main, approved-release promotion, physical/destructive actions, trust-ownership changes, new credentials/permissions, new externally reachable services, commitments and material security-policy choices remain human gates unless explicitly delegated later. Missing tool capability is not treated as a policy approval requirement.

decisions.title: Compact repository state makes AI chat dropouts recoverable
decisions.text: AI_WORK_STATE.md is the first-read checkpoint for fresh or context-degraded sessions. Ordinary turns avoid bulk-reloading history; recovery verifies only volatile facts and selectively loads relevant documents. Context pressure uses empirical GREEN/AMBER/RED proxies rather than a fabricated exact context percentage, and checkpointing is automatic work rather than a human gate.

decisions.title: Native AI project automation is future user-space capability, not model/root authority
decisions.text: After the first usable core prototype, Black Cat may expose the autonomy/recovery pattern as a native project subsystem. Repository policy remains durable authority; a sandboxed operating-system capability broker independently enforces execution boundaries; models are interchangeable bounded workers; local-first/offline operation is preferred; background continuation is user-level/outbound-only; and destructive, trust, credential, protected-merge/release and material-policy boundaries remain explicit human gates.

decisions.title: Reusable AI project policy defaults fail closed
decisions.text: The M26 design now includes a checked-in provider-neutral project seed plus a machine-readable policy schema. The example profile defaults to HUMAN_GATE, network disabled, no inbound listener, no root/raw-device/credential access and explicit forbidden secret/safety/self-expansion actions. Future capability-broker enforcement must validate policy independently of model output and fail closed on mismatch; the current scaffold grants no runtime authority.
